articleTitle: Reliability Rereasch of a MEMS Flow Sensor with Accelerated Degradation Testing
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Ensuring reliability is a key aspect of sensor quality. With the advancement of accelerated degradation testing, it has been widely applied as an efficient strategy to obtain the reliability (life) information on assets. In this article, the reliability test results of a Micro Electro Mechanical System flow sensor based on accelerated degradation testing are researched. Aiming at the reliability problem of this flow sensor's lifetime, temperature stress are considered accelerating conditions. The drifts of flow sensor chip with and are obtained, respectively. On this basis, the Arrhenius model was used by calculating the drift of characteristic parameters to acquire the mean time to failure) of assets in various conditions. In addition, the Weibull Distribution is proved to be the better mode for the flow sensor acceleration life. To verify the rationality of the distribution, the Goodness-of-fit tests were performed using the residual method. The Standard residual error method and Cox-Snell residual error method were used separately, the Anderson-Darling”. value of the Standard residual error and Cox-Snell residual error was 1.728. It proved that the selected life distribution model of this flow sensor with accelerated degradation testing is befitting. This research provides a good way for reliability analysis of thermal mass flowmeter units. Based on those results, we could set up a reliability database for this flow sensor.

articleTitle: Cascades-Risk Informed Transmission Expansion Planning by Behavioural Cloning
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: The growing energy demand, coupled with the increasing trend towards electrification, challenges Transmission Expansion Planning (TEP). In this work, we embrace a risk-informed approach to TEP and address it as a multi-objective optimization problem considering the system risks and the expansion costs. Genetic algorithms, such as NSGAII, are effective in tackling multi-objective optimization problems. We here explore the potential of reinforcement learning as an alternative methodology. Specifically, we used imitation learning techniques to gain insight from prior solutions generated using NSGAII. This novel approach lays the groundwork for future research on reinforcement learning methods, based on policies acquired through imitation learning techniques. By adopting this innovative framework, we anticipate significant advancements in the efficiency and effectiveness of TEP decision-making processes.

articleTitle: Performance Consistency Metric Considering Two-Dimensional Performance Characterization for IGBTs
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: IGBT is a class of power semiconductor device. Due to the limitations of the manufacturing process, the performance of IGBTs is bound to be inconsistent. Further, inconsistent performance will lead to load imbalance when IGBTs are operated in parallel, reducing their reliability. However, the complexity of performance characterization makes it difficult to measure performance consistency for IGBTs. In this paper, the performance of IGBTs is considered comprehensively and the concept of IGBT characteristic function is proposed. On this basis, the performance consistency metric for IGBTs is established. In the application case, performance tests and performance consistency evaluations are carried out on two types of IGBT products.

articleTitle: Optimization Method for an Improved Training of Physics Informed Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Physics Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) are promising methodologies to improve accuracy and extend applicability of Deep Learning in engineering applications, providing a hybrid modeling that combine physics domain knowledge with data-driven methods. Nevertheless, the adoption of PINNs in practice is still limited by the complexity of the training process, where the unbalanced loss gradients in the back propagation step can lead to inaccurate training. This paper discusses a method to improve PINNs training by optimizing the hyperparameters of the model in a standard NN scenario, before applying physics-based constraints, and then balancing the backpropagation by weighting the PINN loss gradients to target the simplified NN loss decay. The result is a faster and improved PINN training that can enable hybrid modeling in industrial applications where both data and domain knowledge are available. A case study is a fluid-dynamics problem taken from literature, described by the Navier Stokes equations that drive thermosenergy processes.

articleTitle: Construction and Application of Double Prevention Mechanism for Highway Operation Safety
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: In order to promote the effective implementation of the double prevention mechanism and curb the occurrence of major accidents on operating highway, the establishment of a double prevention mechanism for operating highway was discussed from the aspects of risk classification management and control and hidden danger investigation and management, the content and process of construction were proposed, and the operating highway were clarified. The specific work in 14 aspects in the three stages of the implementation of the highway double prevention mechanism will further promote the operation unit to move forward the safety production management threshold, and earnestly perform the statutory safety production work responsibilities, so as to improve the management status of operating highway and improve the safety production management level. Reduce operational management costs.

articleTitle: Learning Temporal Truth Tables of Dynamic Fault Trees from Time Series Data on Faults
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Classical fault tree analysis (FTA) can be used to analyze and assess combinations of failures of basic components that lead to system failures within a given system. Classical FTA is however unable to handle how temporal sequences of faults lead to system failures. This is an important issue in complex dynamic systems. To model complex systems where the behavior of components or events depends on the system's state or time, dynamic gates are used. Therefore, we extend our work on learning static repairable fault trees from time series data and propose a data-driven algorithm to extract dynamic gates from time series data of faults. Our proposed algorithm captures sequences of events by converting a time-stamped truth table into temporal gates, which allows learning dynamic gates from data.

articleTitle: A New Temperature and Luminance Combined Degradation Model to Estimate the Lifetime of OLED
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Organic Light Emitting Diodes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{(OLED)}$</tex> have many applications like flat-panel display, curved and foldable displays. However, the biggest technological hurdle against these applications is OLED's short operation lifetime. Many researchers are making efforts to extend the lifetime of OLEDs. Along with the development of new materials and device structures, it is also important to evaluated the lifetime of OLEDs quickly and precisely. In this study, we try to establish the good relationship between the luminance decay of OLEDs and acceleration factors like initial luminance and temperature. The stretched exponential decay model was described in IEC 62341-5-3 and related with the initial luminance. To combine initial luminance and test temperature, we modified the well-known Arrhenius equation and stretched exponential model. The newly developed temperature and luminance combined degradation model could predict the experimental value more accurately than the stretched exponential model in the early stage of degradation. The estimated values became lower than the experimental values in the later stage, but the difference were less than 2 %. Since it is more advantageous to underestimate OLED lifetime than to overestimate it, it could be concluded that the temperature and luminance combined degradation model is more suitable for the OLED lifetime prediction than the well-known stretched exponential decay model.

Author Keywords: temperature and luminance combined degradation model

articleTitle: From Signals to Insights: Uncovering Latent Degradation with Deep Learning as a Stepping Stone Towards Digital Twins of Failures (DTFs)
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: In the study, we investigate the application of deep learning using discretised hydraulic power signals for delineating healthy from non-healthy states on a hydraulic system of a rubber mixing machine. Using the concept of functional-productiveness, the study uses class labels determined as semi-supervised learning by relying on discretised signal behaviour and manually inputted target labels. The feature extraction process is performed through extensive data wrangling to extract discrete-domain features for training the neural networks. The study compares five deep neural network models, in which case the most suitable model is determined by the area under the receiver operator curve (AUC) and the time to train the network. The neural network architecture optimises via Genetic Algorithm (GA). The final result shows that GLobally convergent Resilient PROPagation with Smallest Absolute Gradient (GLPROP-SAG) outperforms other models regarding AUC and time to train the network.

articleTitle: Research on Reliability Evaluation of Emergency System for Operation of Long-Distance Tunnel Sections on Freeways
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: The operation risk of long-distance tunnel section of freeway is high, and the emergency rescue is difficult. Whether the accident can be quickly and effectively rescued determines the severity of the accident consequences to a certain extent. In order to better evaluate the reliability of the emergency system for the operation of long-distance tunnel sections of freeways, considering the characteristics of the emergency rescue of actual tunnel accidents, this paper proposes an evaluation index system for the emergency system for the operation of long-distance tunnel sections of freeways, constructs a model based on analytic hierarchy process, and tests the model through three actual cases. The test results show that the output of the model constructed in this paper is consistent with the actual situation, it can be used to evaluate the reliability of the emergency system for the operation of long-distance tunnel sections of freeways.

articleTitle: A Novel Method for Computing Minimal Cut Sets of Variant-Rich Systems in Fault Tree Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Railway vehicles are considered one of the most important transportation systems for which fault tree analysis can be leveraged to ensure safety and reliability. Computing minimal cut sets of a fault tree in a system is one of the industry's most widely used techniques. Most studies in the field have only focused on specific variants. However, product line engineering and variant management has become an important topic and successful variant management is essential for providing reusability in manufacturing similar products. An essential aspect of variation is the numerous number of variants which increases the required time, space, and complexity for the design and implementation of safe variant-rich systems. This paper proposes a new method for computing minimal cut sets in different variants by considering a 150% model for a set of variants and then removing corresponding basic events in the MCS of the 150% model. The introduced method has been simulated and tested by the FT-MCS library for fault trees with different variables. The results indicate that the presented method computes minimal cut sets for variants efficiently. We have also examined our proposed method in a small case study in railway vehicles. This case study indicates that for calculating MCS of variant products in the industry it is not necessary to compute MCS for each of them and the MCS of the 150% model can be used.

articleTitle: Wear Life Prediction of Spur Gear Transmission System Considering Roughness Influence
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Gear transmission system has the advantage of reliable operation and is used in the mechanical automobile industry. The wear failure of gears will cause significant losses or maintenance costs. Gear wear is influenced by roughness. The existing methods are not accurate enough to predict gear-wearing capacity. A method for predicting the wear life of spur gear transmission systems considering the influence of roughness and dynamic wear coefficient is proposed to calculate the gear wearing capacity. The Archard wear equation is used to analyze the gear wear. The dynamic wear coefficient is modified by the roughness coefficient to evaluate the influence of roughness on wear. A case is analyzed to illustrate the feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Development of Automated Derating Tool for Robust Design
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: This article describes an automated derating tool built within Excel utilizing VBA codes as the solution to adapt customized company derating requirements. Benefits over commercial derating software are specified with standalone executable programs. Tool architecture and main automation functions are explained with methods of incorporating them in Excel using VBA codes.

articleTitle: Importance Analysis Method Application for Feature Selection in a Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Classification is often used method in Machine Learning applications. Different factors cause the efficiency of this method. One of the very important factors is the quality of initial data, which among other things, includes a sufficient, but not excessive, number of input attributes. The procedure for defining a sufficient number of input attributes is known as feature selection. There are approaches to feature selection that form three groups: filter, wrapper, and embedded methods. Filters are used for any classifier and have lower computational complexity. The wrapper methods depend on the algorithm of classifier induction. A classification algorithm evaluates a subset of selected attributes according to a classification measure. These methods have high performance, but they require a lot of computation time to execute. Embedded methods perform attribute selection in the process of the classifier induction and depend on the classifier and algorithm of its induction. In this paper, we propose a new wrapper method based on the well-known approach in reliability analysis which is importance analysis. The proposed method's advantage is the independency of the classifier type and acceptable computational complexity. Therefore, it can be used for any type of classifier and the selected attributes are evaluated by the classification measures that increase the classifier's efficiency.

articleTitle: Drone Fleet Reliability Analysis Based on Uncertain Data Using Binary Decision Diagram
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Drone applications have been developed extensively in different areas. For example, they are used in monitoring, searching, detection, communication, delivery, and transportation of cargo in various sectors of the economy. The reliability of drones in these problems should play a principal role. However the information for the reliability analysis can be incomplete and uncertain. This paper proposes a new method of drone fleet reliability analysis based on uncertain data. The mathematical model of a drone fleet is defined as structure function. The structure function is represented by a Binary Decision Diagram (BDD), which is constructed based on incomplete and uncertain data. The BDD construction is implemented based on the classification method of data mining, in particular, Fuzzy Decision Tree (FDT). This study shows that the transformation of inducted FDT to BDD is simplest than FDT transformation to other forms of structure function representation.

articleTitle: Belief Reliability Evaluation Method Based on Similar Product Information
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Similar product information is valuable for reliability evaluation. How to define and measure similarity is the key to making good use of similar product information. In this paper, a new similarity measurement in terms of margin is newly developed based on the belief reliability theory and similarity system theory. Subsequently, a belief reliability fusion evaluation method is proposed to assess the reliability of the new products in combination with the failure data from the similar old products. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the above methods, a case study of the seed source generation circuit is employed, which shows the proposed methods can reasonably evaluate the reliability based on the fusion data and effectively reduce the uncertainty of the evaluation results.

articleTitle: Physics-Based Machine Learning Hydraulic Piston Pump Performance Degradation and Prognostics
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: The hydraulic piston pump is an important component in the hydraulic system, and it has always been an important problem to accurately and effectively estimate the degradation state of the pump. Physical model-based and data-driven fusion methods can overcome the shortcomings of the two models, and have achieved success in the fields of prognosis and health management. This paper proposes a physics-based deep learning framework for degradation assessment and remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of hydraulic piston pumps. Firstly, the failure physics of the three friction pairs of the hydraulic piston pump is analyzed, and the mathematical calculation formula of the wear amount is obtained. Then, the calculated wear of the three friction pairs is used as the input with physical information, and is fused with the long short term memory (LSTM) network. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by the data of the hydraulic piston pump. It shows that the proposed framework has good capability of degradation assessment and RUL prediction.

articleTitle: Quantifying Reliability in a Complex Safety-Critical System: A Copula and Distorted Distribution Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Complex safety-critical systems (CSCS) play an important role in numerous industries, from aviation and auto-motive to healthcare and nuclear power. In the literature, several approaches have been used to assess the reliability of CSCS when the component lifetimes are independent and identically distributed. However, in real life, systems are composed of multiple types of interdependent components. To address this scenario, in this article, we propose a copula-based approach to examine the reliability of a CSCS that consists of multiple types of components. Our investigation is based on the assumption that components within the same type are interdependent but independent of components of other types. To quantify the dependency among components of the same type, we utilize the Farlie-Gumble-Morgenstern copula, and through minimal cut sets, we derive a distorted distribution that facilitates the assessment of the reliability of CSCS. Finally, we also perform a comparative analysis of the CSCS reliability by considering various values of Kendall's tau and Spearman's rho, which are measures of association between the dependent components. Our results reveal that as the positive (negative) correlation between the components strengthens, the reliability of CSCS tends to decrease (increase).

articleTitle: Machine Learning Model for Predicting Failures in the Context of Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: In general, failure data is obtained in the automotive industry during the warranty period. If these contain the expression of a service life characteristic for each failure, statements can be made about the reliability and availability of the systems. For this purpose, estimation methods are used to adapt empirical lifetime distributions to theoretical lifetime distributions. By means of the distribution characteristics, a prognosis of the reliability and availability to be expected is also possible beyond the observation time. In addition to the data basis to be investigated, which is available completely in test bench and experimental trials or re-censored in the field, various methods can be used for estimation. In the past, several methods have been used, such as the estimators according to Eckel [1], Kaplan-Meier [2] or the estimators according to Pauli [3]. In general, a field failure is subject to several stresses, which can be described by expressions of several lifetime characteristics. For this application case, which occurs in the automotive industry, the known estimation methods, [1]–[3], cannot be used. In this paper, the necessity of multidimensional estimation methods will be introduced first. Then, a new estimation method for multidimensional metrics is presented. In a further step, mathematical proof is given that the new method can provide realistic results. Finally, two example data sets from bench testing and field are presented. Furthermore, some recommendations for the use of the new method are concretized in this context.

articleTitle: A Proposed MIMO Antenna Design for Ultra-Wideband THz Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: In modern wireless communications networks, the demand for new frequency bands is incessantly increasing. One of main promising and feasible resources to be employed in wireless networks technology beyond 5G is the Terahertz frequency band which covers the range from 0.1THz up to 10THz. In this paper, a proposed Ultra-Wideband 2×2 MIMO antenna model for THz applications is introduced. One of the challenges in antenna designs in THz frequency bands is the increasing effect of mutual coupling between the antenna elements which results in a considerable impact on the overall performance of the antenna. Therefore, some techniques are implemented to mitigate the effect of mutual coupling on the performance of the MIMO antenna array such as high isolation, orthogonal positioning, parasitic structures, and loading slots. The proposed model in this paper consists of a 133×255µ<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>rectangular radiator with a circular cut in its middle. It will be shown that this design provides a large bandwidth of around 4.5THz (from 5.5THz up to 10THz), and hence this antenna can be used in high-speed wireless communication networks with high bit rate. Moreover, the performance of the proposed antenna is investigated in terms of various parameters such as Channel Capacity Loss (CCL) and Total Active Reflection Coefficient (TARC) then it is compared with other existing designs. It is found that the proposed model significantly outperforms the existing designs in different aspects.

articleTitle: Resource-Efficient Network for Intelligent Fault Diagnosis Using Tree-Structured Parzen Estimator
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: The fault diagnosis algorithm can timely detect the faults of devices by monitoring their signals, avoiding greater losses. Deep learning has been widely applied in the field of fault diagnosis. However, manually adjusting the network structure and hyperparameters requires expert knowledge and is laborious and time-consuming. In addition, the model structures of most existing deep learning methods are complex and redundant, which is not conducive to operation on hardware devices with limited computational resources. This paper proposes a resource-efficient fault diagnosis method based on Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE). Additionally, a backbone network based on global average pooling (GAP) is proposed. For specific fault diagnosis tasks, the TPE automatically search for hyperparameters, resulting in an optimal model that not only requires low computational resources but also maintains high accuracy levels. Experimental results show that the proposed method can maintain high diagnostic accuracy with lower multiply-accumulate operations (MACs).

articleTitle: Creation of Testing Processes for a Verification of Safety Relevant Vehicle Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: The ISO 26262:2018 standard requires new, more comprehensive test procedures for the development of safety relevant vehicle systems. Complex Safety Mechanisms have an electrical and a software part for the detections and the reaction. The verification for these real-time diagnostics is also complex. One required verification method is the fault injection testing. For this method an appropriate and detailed testing approach is required. This paper shows how to deduce these testing processes for safety relevant vehicle systems. Therefore, the detailed approach is derived. The aim is to create a detailed workflow for all phases for any kind of system modules. As an application example, an automotive project for an actuator control module is considered.

articleTitle: Knowledge-Based AI Model for the Detection of Pinion Wear
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: One common fault on rack-and-pinion drives is wear of the pinion. There are typical characteristics within the recorded sensor signals that can be used as features of an AI approach to monitor this machine failure. Potential hurdles concerning the application of AI models include the lack of labeled data as well as their acceptance and trustworthiness. To address these challenges, this paper pays special attention to the inclusion of expert knowledge and the explainability of the results. The presented approach is an Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) for the detection of pinion wear. Only a small test data set from a healthy machine is used and artificially manipulated with the basic knowledge of experts. It includes the measurements of the motor current and of an accelerometer that is mounted in the gearbox housing as part of a monitoring agent. A survey of experts is used to determine the complex relationship between features and their associated fault conditions. The manipulated dataset and the converted survey results are used for the initialization of the model parameters. It is shown, that with this main usage of domain knowledge and only a small amount of data, an ANFIS model can be set up that already gives a good and explainable estimation of the possibility of a worn out pinion on a rack-and-pinion axis.

articleTitle: Permutation Entropy and Ordinal Patterns as a Resilience Indicator
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Resilience quantification in production systems is essential for making informed decisions. This paper introduces a novel resilience indicator derived from time-series data of system availability. The proposed approach involves symbolic time-series analysis where the availability data is discretized into symbolic sequences. Each symbol in the sequence represents a range of availability values. Using these symbolic sequences, we apply permutation entropy based on ordinal patterns to assess system complexity and resiliency. The methodology is exemplified through a case study involving two production systems with different availability profiles. The symbolic sequences are generated based on predefined thresholds and labeled as “High,” “Medium,” and “Low” availability. Unique ordinal patterns are identified, and their frequencies are calculated to derive the permutation entropy for each system. Special emphasis is placed on dramatic performance declines and spikes, with these events weighted differently in the entropy calculations. Our results indicate that the proposed resilience indicator is computationally efficient and robust to noise and variability, making it ideal for realtime analysis of large datasets. Comparative entropy values provide insights into the relative resilience of the systems under study. The system with lower entropy demonstrated greater regularity and, by extension, higher resilience. This innovative approach promises a new avenue for quantifying resilience in complex systems. Future work will focus on empirical validation in various applications and continuous refinement of the underlying algorithm.

articleTitle: Detection of Anomalous Behaviour of Aircraft Engines for Predictive Maintenance
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: This paper presents a methodology for anomaly detection in aircraft engines on the basis of a survival data formulation. A decision threshold is used for the estimated hazard rate under the assumption of the Cox regression model. Utilization of information relating to aging of the engines gives this formulation a natural advantage over the standard methods of anomaly detection through classification or clustering. There is also the scope of taking into account engine heterogeneity through frailty modeling. The proposed method is found to have superior performance over the standard methods for a data set involving hundreds of flights of about a thousand aircraft engines.

articleTitle: Energy-Efficient Scheduling of Flexible Manufacturing Systems Based on Petri Net
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Flexible manufacturing systems (FMSs) are expected to provide flexibility and efficiency to satisfy the needs of high-variety production of low-volumes. On the other hand, in the current global market competition and energy crisis, reducing energy consumption while maintaining high and flexible productivity is a big challenge for the manufacturing industry. In this paper, a framework for FMS energy-efficient scheduling is proposed. A specific type of petri net model i.e., timed & energy transition petri net (TETPN), is developed for modelling the dynamic production process of FMSs. A TETPN enables model both time and energy characteristics of production operations during manufacturing. A step-wise heuristic algorithm based on hybrid beam search is modified for generating the reachability graph of TETPN. Then an energy-efficient schedule is obtained using the proposed framework. A study case of an FMS producing different types of products is adopted to illustrate the proposed methodology. The results show the efficiency of energy-efficient scheduling of FMSs can, indeed, be achieved.

articleTitle: Cross-Load Generalization of Bearing Fault Recognition with Decision Trees
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: The literature on condition monitoring is nowadays characterized by a wide variety of machine learning approaches. We argue that, in most of the works, the experimental evaluation is conducted in an oversimplified scenario, where training and test data contain samples obtained under the same radial and torsional load conditions. In this paper, we propose to apply an interpretable machine learning model, namely decision trees, to perform fault detection and recognition across different load configurations, a challenging benchmark that requires general-ization capabilities. The rules extracted from the trees provide explanations of the classification process.

articleTitle: Investigating Lipschitz Constants in Neural Ensemble Models to Improve Adversarial Robustness
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: This work investigates the relationship between adversarial robustness and the local Lipschitz constant in ensemble neural network frameworks, namely bagging and stacking. Capitalising on this, we introduce an ensemble neural network design that improves both accuracy and adversarial resilience. We theoretically obtain the local Lipschitz constants for both ensembles, offering insights into their susceptibility to adversarial attacks and identifying architectures optimal for adversarial defense. Notably, our approach negates the need for specific adversarial attack and accommodates any number of pre-trained networks for an ensemble architecture. Evaluations on the MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets against white-box attacks, specifically FGSM and PGD, show our approach is adversarially robust compared to standalone networks and vanilla ensemble architectures.

articleTitle: Reliability Assessment of Large Oil Tanks Considering Variable Correlation
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: For large-scale oil tank structures, the weak areas under seismic effects are determined through stress analysis. Considering the impact of temperature on the fundamental variables and taking into account their correlations, a more precise limit state equation is established. Reliability analysis was conducted on the seismic resistance of the oil tank structure using reliability theory. The failure probabilities of large-scale oil tanks were calculated under different seismic intensities and compared with the Monte Carlo method. The results confirmed the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed model, providing a new method for predicting the reliability of large-scale oil tanks and ensuring their safety and sustainability in seismic conditions.

articleTitle: ASSA-CPS: Automated Formal Safety and Security Assessments in Cyber-Physical Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: This paper describes dissemination and exploitation of the ASSA-CPS industrial research project: Providing both safety and security assessments in emerging technologies, i.e., Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS), is of increasing importance since they are inextricably intertwined. Incorrectly configured and improperly deployed systems are exposed to security threats, and this raises issues in terms of safety. Security vulnerabilities and risks often cause safety hazards. Therefore, safety and security assessment must be considered in combination when companies develop systems to be deployed in wider society. The main idea of this project is to provide companies with a formal approach combining safety and security assessments in a systematic and automatic manner to support the development of trustworthy software systems. Thus, stakeholders become rapidly aware of potential safety and security risks involved in the system development at an earlier stage and apply relevant safety and security protection technologies.

articleTitle: Predicting Endurance Limit in the Probabilistic Fatigue Design of Mechanical Components
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Fatigue damage is a critical concern in mechanical component design, particularly under cyclic loading. Accurate estimation of material endurance limit is essential for ensuring structural reliability and durability. However, conducting large-scale fatigue experiments in practical engineering is often impractical due to time and cost limitations. This paper aims to investigate the relationship between tensile strength and endurance limit, considering factors such as stress, operating conditions, and component geometry. The goal is to improve the accuracy of fatigue strength estimation. Additionally, the study utilizes stress and strength distribution interference to assess reliability. A novel method is proposed for estimating fatigue strength and component reliability.

articleTitle: A New Active Learning Kriging Method for Structural Reliability Based on the Error Analysis of the Predicted Failure Probability
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Currently, a class of methods (AK-MCS) combining active learning Kriging with Monte Carlo simulation (MCS) is promising for structural reliability analysis. The learning function and the convergence criterion are the critical factors affecting the accuracy and efficiency of AK-MCS. In this paper, the error analysis of the predicted failure probability is performed in the framework of AK-MCS, and then a new learning function and convergence criterion are proposed based on the prediction error, which ultimately forms an improved reliability analysis method for AK-MCS. Three examples are employed. Results show that the proposed method in this research can analyze the reliability problems of series system, complex failure domain and finite element engineering with high accuracy, efficiency and robustness.

articleTitle: Performance of Distance Protection of a 132 kV Transmission Line in a Mountainous Area
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: In the Sultanate of Oman, 132 kV overhead transmission lines (OHL) span thousands of kilometers of distance. On these transmission lines, faults occur frequently. Through a distance protection relay, the distance to these faults is calculated. This relay fault distance may not be accurate and the distance error may be significant as a result of fault resistance. Faults are located through the combination of line patrolling, visual inspection, and the reported distance to the fault location. As of now, this process can take anywhere from a few hours to many days in worst-case scenarios. There are several factors that determine how long the fault will take to locate, including fault distance accuracy, the distance from the fault location, the topography in the area, and weather conditions that make visibility difficult. Due to the rapid expansion of the transmission network, OHL faults may be more difficult to locate and identify. This paper analyzes the distance protection performance of a 61.2 km long 132 kV OHL that is partially located in a mountainous area and a desert area. A majority of the insulator faults and other types of faults in Dhofar transmission networks occur on the mountainous part of this line. This study provides valuable information on this transmission line's fault distribution and protection performance.

articleTitle: Thermal Risk Assessment with Mixed Uncertainty Propagation in $\gamma\text{-valerolactone}$ Production
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: This study investigates the propagation of uncertainty on the thermal risk during the production of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma- \mathbf{valerolactone}$</tex> (GVL). It presents a study of mixed uncertainties, which includes aleatoric uncertainty due to inherent variability of the initial conditions and epistemic uncertainty due to a lack of knowledge of the kinetic model. Interval analysis is used for epistemic uncertainty and probabilistic distribution for aleatoric uncertainty. Bootstrap sampling is used for mixing both uncertainty. This study quantifies the propagation of these uncertainties on the thermal risk parameters. It considers how variations in initial conditions and kinetic parameters affect the temperature and temperature ratio. Finally, the probability distributions of the thermal risk parameters under different uncertainties are presented.

articleTitle: A Novel Spatial Sampling Strategy Combining the Kriging Model and Maximin Design for Structural Reliability Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: The Kriging model has been widely explored in structural reliability analysis. Multiple sampling strategies combining the Kriging model are researched to alleviate the computational burden, especially in finite element analysis. In this paper, a novel sampling strategy is proposed to update the Design of Experiments (DoE) by combining Kriging and Maximin design. Maximin design is an experimental design to acquire a spatial distribution matrix. Benefiting from the characteristic of Maximin design, the spatial distance of the selected sample point is taken into account when updating the DoE. The selected sample points are evenly distributed in the sample space, which avoids excessive fitting of the Kriging model. Consequently, the proposed strategy requires relatively few points when constructing the Kriging model, to improve the efficiency of calculation while ensuring accuracy. An explicit example verifys the efficiency and accuracy of the sampling strategy, and a truss structure verifies the outperformance of the proposed method in calculating implicit performance functions.

articleTitle: The Information Propagation Method for Efficient Network Reliability Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: In this paper, we present an ordered message-passing algorithm for propagating information related to system component conditions and dependency between nodes in the target graph network. This tool, called Information Propagation Method, exploits the structure of Directed Acyclic Graphs to assess the reliability of a network. The key advantage of this analytical approach is the computation efficiency obtained by maintaining a priority set of nodes to be updated in each step, every node in the graph is processed as infrequently as possible. Whilst the algorithm converges to an exact solution in simpler graph structures, the solution in more complex graphs is approximated due to the presence of the so-called diamond subgraphs. Diamond subgraphs are identifying solved and recursively decomposed by the algorithm allowing the exploration of complex component dynamics as well as system redundancy strategies. The algorithm is verified against the solution obtained via Monte Carlo simulation. Finally, we discuss a case study example showing the applicability and advantages of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: PNP-Lightweight Model for Predicting Remaining Useful Life of Lithium-Ion Battery to Applying Embedded Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: This paper proposes a Positive & Negative Perceptron (PNP)-Lightweight model prediction method for the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction of Lithium-Ion Battery (LIB) for use in low computation environments such as smartphones and embedded systems. The PNP-Lightweight model is based on the PNP model and has a very low number of trainable parameters. We present a PNP-Lightweight model that can predict the RUL of the LIB using the charge and discharge data of the initial LIB. To prove the superiority of the proposed PNP- Lightweight model, we perform the performance evaluation compared with Long short-term memory (LSTM) and Convolution Neural Network (CNN) models. We build Deep-learning Model using the PNP-Lightweight model (DMP), Deep-learning Model using the LSTM model (DML) and Deep-learning Model using the CNN model (DMC) that can predict the RUL of LIB using the LIB's initial charge and discharge data. To evaluate fairly, we organize the same number of layers and the number of nodes in the hidden layer of the three deep-learning models (DMP, DML, and, DMC) As a result of the performance evaluation, we know that the number of trainable parameters of the DMP is 30 times lower than that of DML and 60 times lower than the DMC. We confirm that the DMP has a lower Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) by 16.18 [cycle] and 3.03 [cycle] compared to the DML and DMC, respectively. In addition, the Symmetric Mean Absolute Percentage Error (SMAPE) of the DMP is 3.6% and 3.96% lower than the DML and DMC, respectively. In addition, we also compare the performance between proposed DMP and CNN+LSTM model. We recognize that performance of proposed DMP is superior to CNN+LSTM model.

articleTitle: Adopting the Specific Operations Risk Assessment Methodology for Drone Inspections at Industrial Sites
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Unmanned Aircraft (or Aerial) Systems (UASs) are attracting an increasing attention from diverse fields (e.g., agriculture, logistics) since they are able to decrease pollution and road congestion. To assure the optimal functioning of these air mobility systems, it is necessary to assess both air and ground risks and manage them for achieving tolerable safety levels. The Specific Operations Risk Assessment (SORA) methodology was developed specifically for such purpose with respect to UAS operations. Although such methodology has been recently applied for assessing risks related to various operations and environments, it has not been employed for operations related to industrial plants. In such a context, this paper investigates a safety risk assessment for drone operations dedicated to inspections in areas within and close to industrial plants. The SORA application to inspection activities in areas within and close to a large refinery allowed determining a medium Specific Assurance and Integrity Level (i.e., the level of confidence that the UAS operation will stay under control), and identifying containment requirements and Operational Safety Objectives. In particular, the involvement of trained and competent operators, and the definition of operational procedures for addressing normal, abnormal, and emergency situations represent necessary measures to ensure safe UAS operations in the setting investigated. The proposed investigation provides only preliminary results that require an in-depth methodological investigation to ensure safe operability of drones in real industrial contexts.

articleTitle: A Prognostic Approach to Improve System Reliability for Aircraft System
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: The primary aims of prognostics encompass the timely detection of potential failures, mitigation or elimination of unscheduled maintenance, prediction of the most suitable timing for preventive maintenance replacement, optimization of maintenance cycles and operational readiness, and enhancement of system reliability by improving design and logistical support for existing systems. In order to facilitate the progress of these approaches, currently available datasets provide a unique and reliable compilation of flight-to-failure trajectories linked to small aircraft engines that have been observed in actual flight conditions. Furthermore, the paper offered an improved neural network that utilized the TanH hyperbolic tangent function. This neural network was enhanced later by integrating it with the TanH, linear, and Gaussian functions. Additionally, a random holdback validation approach was employed in the paper. The results suggest that the NN TanH technique, when implemented, has the potential to significantly enhance the reliability of an aircraft component. This is achieved through accurate estimates of the remaining useful life (RUL) and a proactive understanding of the failure system.

articleTitle: A Resilience Assessment Method for Equipment System-of-Systems (ESoS) Based on Network Percolation
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: The 2022 Russia-Ukraine conflict has revealed that contemporary warfare, characterized by informatization, involves distinct elements of system-of-systems confrontation. Research on the resilience of equipment system-of-systems (ESoS) is crucial for effectively accomplishing combat missions and selecting robust combat forces. This paper presents an assessment method for assessing ESoS resilience based on network percolation. Specifically, the performance of the ESoS is evaluated by quantifying the number of operation loops. Subsequently, the concepts of degradation resilience and recovery resilience are introduced, based on observed changes in ESoS performance. To measure the resilience of the ESoS, a comprehensive resilience metric is proposed based on network percolation. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method is validated using a military case. The analysis results demonstrate that the proposed method not only expands the application scope of percolation theory but also provides a novel approach and perspective for assessing ESoS resilience.

articleTitle: Targeted Symbolic Execution for UAF Vulnerabilities
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Symbolic execution is a popular software testing technique that can systematically examine program code to find bugs. Owing to the prevalence of software vulnerabilities, symbolic execution has been extensively used to detect software vulnerabilities. A major challenge of using symbolic execution to find complicated vulnerabilities such as use-after-free is to not only direct symbolic execution to explore relevant program paths but also explore the paths in a specific order. In this paper, we describe a targeted symbolic execution, called UAFDetect, for finding use-after-free vulnerabilities efficiently. UAFDetect guides symbolic execution to focus on paths that are likely to cause a use-after-free by pruning paths that are unlikely or infeasible to cause that. It uses dynamic typestate analysis to identify unlikely paths and static control flow analysis to identify infeasible paths. UAFDetect performs typestate analysis to detect the occurrence of use-after-free vulnerabilities. Upon the detection of a vulnerability, UAFDetect generates an exploit to trigger the vulnerability. We develop the prototype of UAFDetect and evaluate it on real-world use-after-free vulnerabilities. The evaluation demonstrates that UAFDetect can find use-after-free vulnerabilities effectively and efficiently.

articleTitle: Run Time Memory Error Recovery Process in Networking System
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: System memory errors have always been problematic; today, they cause more than forty percent of confirmed hardware errors in repair centers for both data centers and telecommunications network nodes. Therefore, it is somewhat expected that, in recent years, device manufacturers improved the hardware features to support hardware-assisted fault management implementation. For example, the new standard, DDR5, includes both data redundancy, the so-called Error Correcting Code (ECC), and physical redundancy, the post-package repair (PPR), as mandatory features. Production and repair centers mainly use physical redundancy to replace faulty memory rows. In contrast, field use still needs to be improved, mainly due to a need for integrated system solutions for network nodes. This paper aims to compensate for this shortcoming and presents a system solution for handling memory errors. It is a multi-technology proposition (mixed use of ECC and PPR) based on multi-layer (hardware, firmware, and software) error information exchange.

articleTitle: Fault Tree Analysis and Failure Modes and Effects Analysis for Systems with Artificial Intelligence: A Mapping Study
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Reliability engineering has well-established analysis techniques to design critical systems that will be safe to operate. Two already field-proven techniques are the FTA (Fault Tree Analysis) and the FMECA (Failure Modes, Effects, and Criticality Analysis). These techniques, recommended or required by several supervisory authorities or independent assessments, will continue to be the main assets for the analysis of potential failures and faults. This mapping study revisits FMECA and FTA from the perspective of how they are used when dealing with systems with Artificial Intelligence (AI) components. After the literature database search and selection, 24 primary sources were leveraged to map them regarding their context, scope, considerations, and maturity. The diversity of safety-critical application domains and functions, and the need of more evidences from the evaluations of the proposed approaches, suggest that this field requires a pressing attention. The extracted considerations can be relevant elements of industrial guidelines.

articleTitle: Financial Reduction of Aircraft Maintenance Plan Under Safety and Maintenance Constraints
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: This paper presents a potentially scalable method able to reduce maintenance costs associated with Candidate Certification Maintenance Requirement (CCMR) plans without compromising safety. The failure condition is the floating free caused by the horizontal stabilizer trim actuator (HSTA), which is representative and based on a real case study. An Excel file was created to let the user input the fault tree which was reduced using the cutset theory. In Matlab was developed both the solution algorithm using Matlab heuristic, which takes the Excel file as input, and an interface for the user to input the cost of each maintenance task, latent failure rates, evident failure probabilities, lower and upper bounds, and whether it is flight control. Finally, a cost-benefit analysis was conducted to reduce system latency. The results demonstrated significant cost savings over the life cycle compared to pre-optimization expenses.

articleTitle: Two formal methodologies of Model-Based Safety Assessment for Fault Tree Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: During the design of safety-critical systems, the automatic estimation of the reliability of a proposed architecture could be a valuable asset. In the aerospace sector, according to ARP4754A [17] and ARP4761 [16] standards, the design development process must be performed in parallel with the safety assessment process. The practical reason is that an archi-tecture that does not comply with safety requirements must be modified accordingly as soon as possible. This article illustrates two existing techniques for automatically generating fault tree evaluations from an architectural model. A discussion of their advantages and possible industrial implementation is provided, together with a practical case study.

articleTitle: Verifiable Certificateless Signcryption Scheme for Smart Grids
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Smart Grids (SG) are potential replacements for older power grids, capable of adapting and distributing energy based on demand. The recent technological advances and the increased dependence on electrical energy are all factors in the increased need for reliable and efficient energy systems. The complexity of the smart grid arises from using various components and the high requirements for real-time reliable two-way communication. Accordingly, this represents additional security and privacy challenges. In this paper, we proposed a security and efficient certificateless signcryption scheme with flexible verifiability properties using equality test techniques for Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) within the SG; abbreviated CL-SG. The proposed scheme provides privacy-preserving, confidentiality, data integrity, verifiability, and reduces the level of trust in the third party (e.g., central unit, substation, data concentrator, etc.). The performance evaluation regarding security and complexity analysis shows that the proposed scheme is secure and efficient with good functionality to be fully adopted and implemented within SG. Also, an extended future work is presented to add more flexibility and security properties and features to the current proposed model.

articleTitle: Temperature Compensation in Vibration-Based Structural Health Monitoring Using Neural Network Regression
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Vibration-based structural health monitoring (SHM) systems continuously estimate modal parameters to detect structural anomalies. The modal data corresponding to a healthy state are stored in a database during a training period, forming a baseline for comparison. However, variations in modal frequencies due to environmental and operational factors can lead to larger false positive rates and decrease the sensitivity of system to small damages, reducing the probability of damage detection. To mitigate these challenges, temperature compensation techniques are commonly employed to reduce variations in recorded modal data. In this paper, we propose a temperature compensation technique using neural network regression models. Unlike commonly used multivariate linear regression (MVLR), neural networks can capture the nonlinear relationship between temperature and modal frequencies effectively. The results of the numerical simulation in the present work demonstrate the superiority of the neural network-based compensation over the MVLR approach.

articleTitle: Post-Processing Algorithm for Workplace Safety Risk Monitoring System Based on Deep-Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Surveillance cameras are ubiquitously used as a part of the safety risk monitoring system. Powered by the artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, the system started to detect the anomalies by implementing deep-learning detection models. However, missed or unexpected warnings are happening frequently. And thus this problem is considered as a major flaw to the AI safety risk monitoring system. This study proposes a post-processing algorithm called PDAR aiming to enhance the accuracy of workplace safety risk monitoring system powered by deep-learning models. The PDAR consists of 3 types of algorithms with 3 typical situations: making warning when an action or an object detected, making warning when an absence or an inaction detected and making warning when joint objects or actions detected. The warning accuracy is significantly increased with PDAR validated with intensive experiments. An improvement of warning accuracy from 55.15% to 98.53% was observed in the test result. Moreover, an evaluation framework is also introduced which evaluate the warning accuracy by considering the missed warning and unexpected warning equally since either a missed warning or an unexpected warning would make serious consequences in safety risk monitoring scenarios. The dataset used in the experiments are now open sourced at: www.github.com/freelectry/PDAR.

articleTitle: Deadlock- and Starvation-free Formally Verified Client Library for Robots
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Robot middleware is crucial for managing diverse robotic functions, though it often faces issues like deadlock and starvation. Addressing these, this paper introduces two libraries, safe_drive and async_lib, aiming to enhance the efficiency and safety of ROS 2 middleware. These libraries address deadlock and starvation through well-typed APIs and formal verification methods, offering enhanced security. The safe_drive library, a single-threaded client library for ROS 2, features a task executor verified to be free from deadlock and starvation using PlusCal and TLA+, establishing credibility. On the other hand, async_lib offers well-typed intra-process communication APIs for multi-threading environments, with ver-ified multi-threaded executors that support safe_drive in complex applications, thereby facilitating efficient robot applications. Furthermore, the paper proposes using session types and typestate programming for safe communication protocol im-plementation, capable of detecting protocol violations at both compile and run time, especially useful in complex scenarios like state transitions in action servers where violations could lead to deadlock.

articleTitle: Modelling and Analysis of the Scheduled Maintenance for the Test Cell of the IFMIF DONES Facility
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: This paper emphasizes the significance of maintenance for ensuring the efficiency and reliability of irradiation facilities, specifically focusing on the Test Cell in the International Fusion Materials Irradiation Facility DEMO Oriented Neutron Source (IFMIF DONES) facility. We propose a comprehensive methodology that combines Petri nets modelling and regression analysis to develop an effective maintenance plan. Regression analysis generates precise linear equations, serving as surrogate models for Petri nets simulations, significantly reducing computational time. Using these fitted regression equations, we rapidly estimate the Test Cell system's availability, uptime, and downtime, offering valuable insights for enhancing reliability, maintenance planning, and system safety. The paper presents the results of regression analysis and the findings of Petri nets modelling simulations, providing an efficient maintenance scheme for the Test Cell.

articleTitle: Runtime Safety Assurance of Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: The paper deals with runtime safety assurance of autonomous vehicles (AVs), First, we closely examine the current state of AV technology, highlighting the incredible progress made by industry leaders in ensuring minimal risks in their vehicles. Our analysis of reported disengagements in AVs reveals interesting insights, showing that most disengagements are initiated by human test drivers rather than by the AV systems themselves and that they often occur on streets and freeways. Next, to ensure AVs' safety, we explored various safety architectures, including 1oo2, 1oo2D, and 2oo3, and thoroughly evaluated their reliability. We also introduce the concept of runtime safety assurance (RTA), a system that closely monitors the AV's state and employs emergency measures through a backup controller if the safety conditions are breached. Such a safety architecture - having separate safety and performance loops - has several benefits, which are highlighted in this paper. Furthermore, we emphasize the crucial role of robust sensing and perception systems in AVs, showing that multi-modal sensing and sensor fusion can effectively enhance the system reliability. We validated the reliability of these systems through extensive software testing and comparisons with ground-truth data. Finally, we explore fault-detection techniques for AVs by employing simulations to detect and handle faults in the control system.

articleTitle: Study on the Application of Graph Theory Algorithms and Attack Graphs in Cybersecurity Assessment
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Postulating the behavior of attackers is important in the design of cybersecurity protection measures. Attack graph is a technique employed for this purpose, which aids in identifying and modeling the potential attack paths an attacker could take to gain unauthorized access to a cyber network, exploit vulnerabilities, and compromise the system's confidentiality, integrity, and availability. In this study, we propose a framework aimed at identifying potential attack paths and determining the shortest path with the highest probability of a successful attack. Meanwhile, based on the attack graph determine the minimum patch sets with the most severity to protect the network security. Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) is utilized to quantify the exploitability and severity of each vulnerability. The Dijkstra algorithm is utilized to calculate the shortest path with the highest probability, and the Stoer-Wagner algorithm is utilized to calculate the minimum patch sets with the most severity. To demonstrate the proposed framework, we apply it to a simplified SCADA system within a corporate network susceptible to cyber attacks.

articleTitle: Semi-supervised Learning for Source Code Function Classification Using Hierarchical Density-Based Clustering
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: In the field of software development, source code topic classification is critical for program comprehension and software maintenance. Source code topic classification is a challenging task that involves classifying software artifacts into predefined topics. Traditional supervised learning approaches require a large amount of labeled data, which is often expensive and time-consuming to obtain. In this paper, we explore the application of semi-supervised learning techniques for source code and propose a semi-supervised learning approach that leverages both labeled and unlabeled data to improve the accuracy of source code topic classification. We utilize hierarchical density-based clustering to group similar source code artifacts, and then apply semi-supervised learning techniques to assign topics to these code functions. Experimental results on a real-world dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed approach in achieving high accuracy and less complexity, which is due to using semi-supervised learning.

articleTitle: Reliability, Availability, Maintainability and Inspectability (RAMI) Analysis Supporting the Design of ITER Ancillary Systems for Tritium Breeding
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: The ITER research facility is an excellent example of a complex system, requiring a structured analysis of its Reliability, Availability, Maintainability and Inspectability (RAMI) performance. In particular, this paper is focused on the Water Cooled Lithium-Lead Tritium Breeding Module (WCLL-TBM), which is one of the systems under development for the self-breeding of tritium to be tested in ITER. The reliability and availability targets of ITER shall be achieved also considering the failures of the WCLL-TBM components. Moreover, the reliability and availability of the WCLL-TBM shall be evaluated with reference to its capability to carry out the required main function, which is to demonstrate and test the breeding of tritium. This paper describes the process followed for the RAMI analysis of the WCLL-TBM Ancillary systems, highlighting the compelling need for parallelism and iterations with the design activities and with the specification of the maintenance strategy, and providing an overview of the key design aspects, of the main difficulties and challenges encountered, and of the improvements achieved.

articleTitle: An Industry-Based Survey on Development and Integration of Safety Element out of Context
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: ISO 26262 introduced the concept of Safety Element out of Context (SEooC), a generic element which is developed to be used across many applications, hence, saving a lot of time, effort, and cost. The objective of this paper is to report about the industrial experience applying the SEooC approach. The knowledge about the good practice of this approach is limited regardless of its recommendation by ISO 26262. An industry-based survey was carried out, consisting of two parts: (i) description of the target group and challenges in functional safety and (ii) the SEooC approach.

articleTitle: Safety 4.0: Model-Based Approach Toward Perpetual Flight with an Autonomous, Solar-Powered Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Skydweller is an American-Spanish company in pursuit of perpetual flight. In 2019, it acquired Solar Impulse 2 as a flying testbed, a 72-meter wingspan solar-powered aircraft with reversible flight controls. Ever since, the aircraft has been continuously modified and flight tested in Albacete, Spain, to achieve a large, uncrewed, fully autonomous platform capable of perpetual endurance operations. This aircraft represents a challenge from the safety point of view due to different factors, such as design complexity, operational aspects, and cybersecurity risks, among others. This aircraft includes a wide variety of complex systems, multiple ground stations with different levels of involvement and different kinds of payloads, as well as cutting-edge technologies and the integration of components that are not purely aeronautical. The operational aspects also contribute to a high demand on safety analyses due to the time the aircraft will remain in the air and the distance from the bases of operation. Moreover, the nature of the missions that this aircraft can do (border surveillance, telecommunications, and other government, security, or firefighting missions, among others) raises certain cybersecurity risks that must be addressed to assure the overall safety of the aircraft. Skydweller uses a model-based approach to address complex issues affecting near perpetual endurance while providing a flexible safety framework for rapid development. This approach is founded on standard aviation industry practices and optimized for execution in a multinational start-up environment where analysis products must be applicable to multiple airworthiness authorities. It constitutes an implementation of Model-Based Safety Assessment for a safety-critical application in a fast development environment, where the safety case is completely integrated within the model assuring consistency and avoiding discrepancies through a single source of truth. To minimize change impact and optimize testing of the autonomous systems, Skydweller uses the concept of “Safety Boundary”, defined as the set of equipment that constitutes a minimal justified airworthy configuration, anchored for this phase, by the presence of a safety pilot on board the airframe with full control of the aircraft if necessary. The Safety Boundary concept has allowed a safety critical assessment of the human-rated full authority digital fly-by-wire system while allowing a faster, lower cost assessment of non-critical systems under development. This model-based approach allows Skydweller to produce all the safety artifacts, required by ARP 4754A and ARP 4761 (FHA, PASA/PSSA, ASA/SSA, CCA,…), that are used as Acceptable Means of Compliance for multiple airworthiness authorities, utilizing a team of two safety engineers. The effectiveness of the approach has been demonstrated before the airworthiness authorities (AESA), obtaining a permit to fly for a modified human-rated fly-by-wire system that allowed Skydweller to perform fully automated flights with the safety pilot onboard.

articleTitle: Railway Infrastructure Resilience Analysis in Case of Flooding: Case Study in Italy
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: This study seeks to assess the flooding impacts on Italy's railway infrastructure, to establish a model based on which the system vulnerability can be measured, and the mitigation strategy can be evaluated. Using Python libraries, exposed railway sections are determined by intersecting flood risk map with Italy's railway network. In addition, Eurostat's dataset provides traffic statistics for weighing network sections. The whole project comprises three phases: i) identifying flood-exposed railway elements, ii) transferring traffic data to the real-path link dataset and assigning weights to nodes according to traffic. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), focusing on system resilience to flooding, are using Degree Centrality (DC) and Betweenness Centrality (BC). These outcome related KPIs aid in understanding and mitigating the impact of disruptions, enhancing railway system resilience.

articleTitle: Using Sensitivity Analysis and Search-Based Testing in the Verification of a Computer Vision Function
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: For operating safely, autonomous robots and automated driving applications need to reliably detect objects in their environment under a huge variety of external conditions. Previous works introduced the usage of semantic domain models for capturing important domain parameters that have an impact on detection performance of perception systems. In these approaches, rating the importance of domain parameters is usually left to the intuition and experience of a test engineer. In this paper, we present a framework utilizing global sensitivity analysis (GSA) for determining the impact of domain parameters on detection performance and exploiting search-based testing (SBT) technology for generating difficult input images for testing a computer vision function based on the domain parameters identified by GSA. In addition, we discuss the benefits and lessons learned of the interplay of GSA and SBT for testing a perception function. In our evaluation, we apply our framework on a pedestrian detection use case from the automated driving domain. Our evaluation results show that SBT finds critical test images faster than random testing and that selecting the right domain parameters based on GSA is crucial for good test results.

articleTitle: A Practical Approach for Reliability Prediction of Safety Critical Software Using Multi-Model Ensemble Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel and comprehensive approach for estimating the reliability of safety critical software components in autonomous vehicle motion systems. The proposed approach in this paper presents a combination software reliability model (CSRM) that integrates multiple non-homogeneous Poisson process (NHPP) software reliability growth models (SRGMs) to achieve a reasonable compromise between accuracy, the trade-off between the goodness of fit and the simplicity, and stability. By using machine learning techniques, the CSRM effectively combines the strengths of individual SRGMs while mitigating their weaknesses through suitable evaluation and calibration techniques. The developed CSRM has been successfully applied and validated to facilitate a smoother and more efficient evaluation of reliability targets for software components in autonomous robotic wheelchair (ARW). Based on the validation results, the new CSRM has significantly enhanced the efficiency of the process for evaluating whether the defined reliability goals were being achieved. Furthermore, has facilitated a more accurate assessment of the need for further test executions and better planning of the required verification and validation session. This new approach provides valuable insights into the reliability of the developed software, particularly for software developers lacking extensive experience in identifying and applying appropriate SGRM.

articleTitle: Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Turbofans with Virtual Health Indicator: A Comparison of Particle Filter-Based Approaches
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: The accurate estimation of the remaining useful life plays a crucial role in ensuring the reliability and efficiency of turbofan engines. In this study we address this objective by resorting to a virtual health indicator, previously developed by the authors for the estimation of the turbofan state of health, which is propagated in the future for estimating the engine end of life. The proposed approach consists in a combination of a multi-layer perceptron whose parameters are identified by a particle filter, in which the network act as a surrogate model for the hidden degradation state. The model is initialized on the basis of known degradation trajectories, and is recursively updated by the particle filter when new observations are available, providing flexibility to the method. To assess the effectiveness of the proposed approach, a comparison is made with a commonly used combination in the literature, which utilises a particle filter and a sum of two exponential functions. The results of the comparison demonstrate that the new approach achieves at least comparable results, and in the majority of cases, it outperforms the usual combination.

articleTitle: Controller Placement with Respect to Controller Reachability
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: In this paper we investigate the controller placement problem on networks using controller reachability as the network performance metric. This metric is defined as the probability that each node can reach at least one controller, given that each link is operational with a fixed probability. By exploring placements for more than 100 real-world networks and by varying the number of controllers from two to five, we find that controller reachability varies greatly with different placements. Obviously, increasing the number of controllers increases the controller reachability. However, the extent of this increase depends on the strategy with which the controllers are placed. The findings indicate that efficient controller placement strategies should be developed to ensure good network performance. In this research, we propose four controller placement strategies. One strategy is based on topological network metrics: node degree and path length between controllers and nodes. The other three heuristic strategies are the greedy algorithm, the classic genetic algorithm and the heuristic genetic algorithm.
